lessons.title: Be a guest at a home dinner
lessons.objective: Ask what gift to bring, how and when to arrive, and what table manners are expected.
lessons.focus: 手土産 is a gift taken to someone’s home; お土産 is usually a gift brought back from a trip. ～ばいいですか asks what one should do: 何を持っていけばいいですか。伺う is a humble way to say “visit”: 何時ごろ伺えばいいですか。With a friend, ～ないでね is a casual request. Lucía says うちの家族では to specify her own family’s custom of arriving 15 minutes after the stated dinner time. 食後のおしゃべり describes conversation after the meal.
lessons.scene: Tonight Mark visits his friend Lucía’s parents for dinner in Puebla. He asks what gift to bring, when to arrive, and what to do at the table. Lucía suggests wine or dessert because her mother loves sweets. Dinner is at 8, and Lucía says arriving 15 minutes late is normal in her family. She asks Mark to wait for her parents to begin eating, keep his napkin on his lap, and stay for conversation after dessert. Mark buys dessert at a pastry shop and flowers for the hosts.

forms.question: 持っていきますか
forms.example: 手土産を持っていきます。

forms.question: 伺いましょうか
forms.example: 何時ごろ伺えばいいですか。

forms.question: 待ちますか
forms.example: ご両親が食べ始めるのを待ちます。

forms.question: 持ってきますか
forms.example: よかったら、ワインを一本持ってきて。

forms.question: 着きますか
forms.example: ご両親の家に着きます。

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 今夜、マークはプエブラにある友だちのルシアの両親の家で夕食をごちそうになります。
reader.en: Tonight Mark is going to have dinner at the home of his friend Lucía's parents in Puebla.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: まず、ルシアに「何を手土産に持っていけばいいかな」と聞きます。
reader.en: First he asks her: What gift can I bring?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: ルシアは「よかったらワインを一本かデザートを持ってきて。母は甘い物が大好きだから」と答えます。
reader.en: Lucía answers: If you want, bring a bottle of wine or a dessert, because my mom loves sweets.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: マークは「何時ごろに行けばいいかな」とも聞きます。
reader.en: Mark also wants to know: What time should I arrive?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: ルシアは「夕食は8時だけど、うちの家族では15分遅れて来るのが普通だよ」と言います。
reader.en: Lucía tells him: Dinner is at 8, but in my family arriving 15 minutes late is normal.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: それからマークは「食卓でしてはいけないことはある？」と聞きます。
reader.en: Then Mark asks: Is there anything I shouldn't do at the table?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: ルシアは家族のマナーを説明します。「両親が食べ始めるまで待って、ナプキンはひざの上に置いてね」。
reader.en: Lucía explains her family's manners: Wait for my parents to start eating and keep your napkin on your lap.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 「それに、両親は食後のおしゃべりが好きだから、デザートのすぐあとに帰らないでね」。
reader.en: Also, my parents enjoy the after-dinner conversation, so don't leave right after dessert.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: マークは笑顔で、洋菓子店でデザートを買い、招いてくれたご両親への花も買って、手土産を用意してルシアの両親の家に着きます。
reader.en: Mark smiles, buys a dessert at a pastry shop and some flowers for the hosts, and arrives with his gift ready.

lessons.internalReviewNote: AI-assisted owner-only draft. Haiku 5.5 was requested for the first candidate, but CLI metadata reported Sonnet 5.5; do not count that as Haiku verification. First Opus call timed out. Second Opus 5.5 read-only critique found an imprecise help offer, awkward 伺いますか, missing source verb/term coverage, register differences, and source-fidelity issues. Self-check corrected help offer, forms, source terms, family-specific arrival wording, and purchase locations. Reader remains casual friend dialogue; cards provide polite alternatives for practice, and host-directed thanks is an additional Japanese-specific phrase. Qualified Japanese and dining-domain review remains open.
